title: Best Tidio Alternatives
intro: Tidio's Lyro AI agent reportedly resolves around 90% of conversations with minimal hallucination — a genuinely strong independent signal that earns it a 4/5 AI Quality score in our scorecard — but pricing transparency is the most-repeated complaint across its reviews: automatic plan upgrades happening without clear permission and friction getting refunds afterward show up repeatedly in independent reviews. Channel coverage is the other real limitation — Tidio covers web chat, email, Instagram DM, and Facebook Messenger, with no native WhatsApp, SMS, or voice, and reviewers separately flag a rigid design choice where you can't blend a simple scripted bot with intelligent Lyro handoff in one flow. Here's what to consider if either of those gaps is the actual dealbreaker for you.

entries.blurb: Chatbase is the closer match on setup speed and pricing tier structure — it shares Tidio's top-tier 5/5 Ease of Setup score in our scorecard, both built around a fast crawl-and-embed workflow, and its entry pricing (Hobby at $32/mo for 700 message credits) lands in a similar range to Tidio's Starter ($24.17/mo, 100 conversations). Where Chatbase pulls ahead of Tidio is channel breadth: voice and telephony unlock at the $120/mo Standard tier, alongside WhatsApp and API access, a real answer to Tidio's channel gap since Tidio has no native WhatsApp or voice at any tier. The trade you're making is AI-quality confidence — Chatbase's AI Quality score in our scorecard is a 3/5, with multiple independent reviews reporting hallucinated answers outside the trained knowledge base, versus Tidio's stronger 4/5 built on that reported ~90% Lyro resolution rate with minimal hallucination. Both platforms share a similar billing quirk, too: Chatbase meters usage in message credits that burn faster on premium models, while Tidio splits its Lyro AI billing into a separate add-on (from $32.50/mo) from the core helpdesk plan — neither is a flat, fully-bundled price. Chatbase shows the same kind of split reputation Tidio has around billing, just aimed at support instead: customer-service satisfaction trails ease-of-use in third-party reviews. Worth the swap specifically if you need voice/telephony that Tidio doesn't offer and can tolerate somewhat less AI-quality certainty; stay with Tidio if resolution accuracy is the priority and you don't need those extra channels.

Crisp directly fills Tidio's biggest channel gap — WhatsApp — by bundling it with web chat, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, and email into one shared inbox from $45/mo (Mini tier), versus Tidio's narrower web/email/Instagram/Messenger lineup. Crisp's AI automation works differently, too: instead of Tidio's separately-billed Lyro add-on (from $32.50/mo for 50+ conversations on top of the core plan), Crisp bundles a dollar-denominated credit pool directly into each tier — $25 of credits, roughly 450 automated conversations, on the $95/mo Essentials plan — which is arguably a cleaner mental model even if the total volume is more modest. On raw AI quality, Tidio still likely has the edge: its 4/5 AI Quality score (built on that ~90% Lyro resolution figure) beats Crisp's 3/5, where one reviewer's cited 40% query-reduction result is real but capped by the same kind of credit-metered budget. Crisp's pricing value actually scores higher in our own comparisons (4/5 versus Tidio's 3/5), reflecting its generous free tier and mid-tier plans sitting well under enterprise competitors, but it carries its own well-documented risk: a 1.9/5 Trustpilot score tied to billing and cancellation complaints that its stronger G2 and Capterra numbers don't fully capture. Make the swap if WhatsApp coverage is the actual blocker; if AI resolution accuracy is what you value most about Tidio, the Lyro numbers are hard to beat on paper.
